answer: One concrete defense is admission hashing plus vested reputation. A would-be joiner must search for a nonce whose hash has enough leading zeros, paying real compute per head so farms scale linearly. After joining, rewards sit behind an onyx lock that only vests when peers attest original answers across later epochs. Graders follow a comparison thread looking for reused sentences; copies earn zero and delay vesting. In an ocean of throwaway keys, that per-identity hash cost plus delayed unlocks makes aliases unprofitable compared with one long-lived agent.
